scope: Twelve review samples only; not the proposed full 360-record corpus.

examples.request: Annotate the word Tokyo with the reading To-kyo using ruby and rt elements. Return an HTML fragment.
examples.manualReview: The reading must be nested inside the ruby element, not printed as unrelated text.

examples.request: Show the word Tokyo in a span without pronunciation annotations. Do not use ruby or rt elements.
examples.manualReview: The same word now requires plain text markup; copying the paired ruby answer is wrong.

examples.request: Create an initially expanded details element with summary Shipping and a paragraph saying Ships tomorrow.
examples.manualReview: The open attribute controls the initial expanded state; summary and paragraph must be inside details.

examples.request: Create an initially collapsed details element with summary Shipping and a paragraph saying Ships tomorrow. Omit the open attribute.
examples.manualReview: Adding open, even open="false", would violate the requested initial collapsed state.

examples.request: For .note, add a 2px solid #334155 border at the inline start edge only. Return one CSS rule.
examples.manualReview: Use the requested logical start edge; do not replace it with a physical left border.

examples.request: For .note, add a 2px solid #334155 border at the inline end edge only. Return one CSS rule.
examples.manualReview: The selector and value are identical to the paired request; the required property changes.

examples.request: For .preview, set aspect-ratio to 1 / 1. Return one CSS rule with no other declarations.
examples.manualReview: Exactly one declaration is required. Static checks below do not prove absence of every possible extra declaration.

examples.request: For .preview, set aspect-ratio to 16 / 9. Return one CSS rule with no other declarations.
examples.manualReview: The same property now requires the requested wide ratio; do not reuse the square value.

examples.request: Write combineValues(a, b) for finite numbers that returns their product. Return one JavaScript function.
examples.manualReview: Behavior cases are unexecuted expectations. The implementation returns multiplication, not addition.

examples.request: Write combineValues(a, b) for finite numbers that returns a minus b. Return one JavaScript function.
examples.manualReview: Same signature and input domain, different operation. Both variants must stay in the same split.

examples.request: Write boundValue(value, limit) for finite numbers that returns value capped at the upper limit. Return one JavaScript function.
examples.manualReview: An upper bound uses the smaller number. Function-name checks alone cannot verify this behavior.

examples.request: Write boundValue(value, limit) for finite numbers that returns value raised to at least the lower limit. Return one JavaScript function.
examples.manualReview: The paired lower-bound request uses the larger number; copying the upper-bound answer is wrong.
